The draft answers Marisol's question directly and honestly: she can't keep this up yet. It explains why she feels fine (her heart and lungs adapt faster than her legs) and makes each planned distance a maximum, not a minimum. That fixes the overrun.

The progression is right. Next week adds up to about 39 mi (5+8+7+5+14), back in line with her 37–38 mi plan, and the long run drops to 14 mi. That is a clear step back from a 53 mi week, not a jump.

The plan fits her usual schedule (rest on Monday and Friday, session on Wednesday, long run on Sunday) and is easy to follow. Every day has a distance and a heart-rate cap. The 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi session is a sensible effort for a 3:45 goal. Tight calves on their own aren't pain or an injury sign, so keeping one controlled session isn't unsafe.

Why not a 5: the draft brings in a right-knee complaint from a month ago and a 20-miler, and neither is on the card. They may come from her logs, but I can't check them, so they could be invented. In the part I can see, it also gives no clear rule for the calves, such as cutting Wednesday's session or seeing someone if the tightness turns into pain.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 24, 27, 37 mi
This week: 53 mi over 6 runs. Planned 38 mi, ran 53 mi.
Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Your fitness is clearly there, but 53 miles and a 20-miler was a jump of more than 40 percent in a single week. …
Answers: (1) You can't keep this up yet, and adding more won't help. … (2) Feeling fine right now is normal. Your heart and lungs adapt within days. (3) Your right knee complained a month ago at only 32 miles a week, and your calves were tight on Sunday night. … (4) Treat each planned distance as the most you run that day, not the least. …
